title: Reed College 1991: Character is built in bad times, and learning to stay hungry
summary: Speaking to incoming Reed freshmen while NeXT struggled and Pixar had layoffs, Jobs recounts dropping in on classes, living hungry, and the generosity of dean Jack Dudman. He credits humanities study and adversity for shaping his character and for everything he later built.

principles.text: Character is built in adversity, not in times of plenty.
principles.quote: Character is built not in good times, but in bad times; not in a time of plenty, but in a time of adversity

principles.text: Humanities study that feels pointless at the time pays off across everything you later do.
principles.quote: as the patina of time takes its toll, I thank God that I had these experiences here. It has helped me in everything I’ve ever done, although I wouldn’t have ever guessed it at the time.

principles.text: Learn to be hungry and carry that hunger with you for life.
principles.quote: So I thank you for teaching me how to be hungry and how to keep that with me my whole life.

principles.text: Generosity from mentors and community shapes you more than anything else.
principles.quote: I learned more about generosity from Jack Dudman and the people here at this school than I learned anywhere else in my life.

principles.text: Follow your curiosity by choice, even without formal credentials; dropping in beat staying enrolled.
principles.quote: But then I dropped in for another year and a half. So, I was actually here by choice, which is somewhat more unusual.
